Restored and annotated editions

The Golem

Gustav Meyrink

A new translation

Complete, and free. Until now it could not be both.

Read more

Gustav Meyrink’s The Golem appeared in 1915 and sold on the order of two hundred thousand copies in its first year. It is not the folk tale. There is no clay servant taking orders. There is a man who cannot be certain whose memories he is having, a ghetto being demolished around him while he works, and a figure that returns to Prague every thirty three years wearing whatever face the city needs it to wear.

The English situation has been peculiar for a century. The only unabridged translation most readers can name is still in copyright. The translation that entered the public domain, made in 1928, is widely reported to be a cut text. A reader has had the choice of a Golem that is complete but not free, or free but not complete.

This is a new translation, made from the 1915 Kurt Wolff text. Complete and unabridged, all nineteen chapters.

This annotated edition contains:

A new, complete English translation of the 1915 original

An original introduction: the hat that frames the whole novel, the two months Meyrink spent in a cell in 1902 and what they did to the prison chapters, and the real ghetto that was being pulled down while the book was being serialised

A note on the translation, setting out what was kept, what was deliberately left in German, and one clear error in the original that has not been corrected

A headnote before each of the nineteen chapters

A glossary of the Kabbalistic, Yiddish and Bohemian vocabulary Meyrink assumed his readers shared with him, which says plainly where he is inventing and where he is not

An appendix: the 1847 Prague version of the Golem legend, also newly translated, which Meyrink read and which the novel argues with

There is only one true waking, and that is the one you are now approaching.

What this edition adds

  • A new, complete English translation from the 1915 German text
  • An Introduction, a note on the translation, and a headnote for each chapter
  • A glossary of about 33 entries
  • A newly translated appendix: the 1847 Golem legend
